hook: Earthquake scales, the loudness of sound in decibels and the brightness of stars all use logarithms, because each covers a range of millions or billions. A log turns "a thousand times bigger" into "3 more". Chemistry uses the same trick for quantities that change by powers of ten.

prereq.why: Move the point 4 places right to reach 4.7, so the exponent is −4.

figure.caption: A logarithm is the exponent: each step of 1 on the log scale is a factor of 10 in the number.

chain.cause: A logarithm is the exponent that 10 must be raised to

chain.effect: the log of a product is the sum of the logs, so a factor of 10 adds 1

chain.cause: The natural log uses base e (about 2.718) instead of 10
chain.effect: ln x = 2.303 log x, and mixing them up gives answers 2.303 times off

chain.cause: An antilog raises the base to the log
chain.effect: 10ˣ undoes log and eˣ undoes ln

ideas: log x (base 10) is the power of ten that gives x: log 10⁻⁵ = −5. Numbers between 0 and 1 have negative logs.
log (A × B) = log A + log B; log (A/B) = log A − log B; log (Aⁿ) = n log A.
ln x is the natural log, base e. ln x = 2.303 log x. Use the key the equation names.
Digits after the decimal point in a log are its significant figures: log (3.2 × 10⁻⁴) = −3.49. Undo log with 10ˣ and ln with eˣ (the antilog).

misconception.wrong: log and ln are two names for the same button, so either one works.
misconception.right: They use different bases. ln x is 2.303 times log x, so using the wrong one makes the answer 2.303 times off. Equations that say ln need LN; equations that say log need LOG.

summary: A base-10 logarithm is the exponent of ten that gives a number; the natural logarithm uses base e. Logs turn multiplying into adding, so a factor of ten adds 1 to log x. ln x = 2.303 log x. An antilog undoes a log: 10ˣ for log, eˣ for ln. The decimal places of a log match the significant figures of the number.
